name: Jessica Pratt
label: Mexican Summer
lede: Jessica Pratt recorded her first songs on analogue tape in 2007 and left them unreleased for five years. By 2024 she was closing a Chanel couture show, playing Colbert and singing on an A$AP Rocky single.

eras.title: A kid in Redding with a borrowed guitar
eras.text: Pratt grew up in Redding, California, with a mother who played her Tim Buckley, X and the Gun Club. By 16 she was recording at home, for nobody in particular.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician) · Stereogum: Q&A Jessica Pratt
years.h: Jessica Pratt is born in Redding, California
years.p: Her mother, an astrologer, plays her Tim Buckley, X and the Gun Club.
years.xp: She grew up in Redding with her mother, who kept a wide run of records going. Stereogum's telling is that she was technically homeschooled, though she has said it was mostly because she had no interest in school.

years.h: A brother's Stratocaster and a T. Rex record
years.p: At 15 she learns guitar on her older brother's Stratocaster, playing along to Electric Warrior (1971).
years.xp: At 16 she was recording songs at home with her mother's Fender amp and a microphone, according to Wikipedia. Home recording stayed her method: her second album was cut on a Tascam 4-track.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (album) · Exclaim!: Jessica Pratt Talks
years.h: She records the songs, then lets five years go by
years.p: The tracks that become her debut are cut on analogue tape in 2007, at a friend's friend's studio.
years.xp:
She told Exclaim! the studio belonged to a friend's friend who "just had some free time". The plan, in her words: "let's go down there and work quickly and just record all the stuff you have lying around."

The tapes stayed unreleased until Tim Presley heard them.

eras.title: A label for one record
eras.text: Tim Presley of White Fence heard her recordings in San Francisco and started Birth Records to put them out. Nobody expected the label to do anything else.

years.big: "He really did it out of the goodness of his heart."
q: He really did it out of the goodness of his heart.
years.src: Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician) · Exclaim!: Jessica Pratt Talks
years.h: Tim Presley starts a label for one record
years.p: Pratt on [[Tim Presley|25f6404b-4738-48a2-b1e0-465b7430fb93]] of [[White Fence|68548de4-c045-426a-9745-b52a8a22d2d2]], who founded Birth Records to release her tapes. She says he had no plans to do anything else with it.
years.xp:
Presley's brother was her roommate in San Francisco for three years. Presley heard the recordings and started the label, which Wikipedia says was founded specifically to release her music.

Pratt told Exclaim! it was "just a means to an end."

years.src: Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (album) · Stereogum: Q&A Jessica Pratt · Drag City: Jessica Pratt
years.h: The debut sells its 500 copies in under two weeks
years.p: Pitchfork, Consequence of Sound and PopMatters all cover a record from a label that exists only to release it.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Pitchfork rated it 7.5 and Metacritic averaged 78 from seven critics. The Boston Globe compared its fingerpicked intimacy to Sibylle Baier. PopMatters was more mixed, finding the production made some words hard to make out.

Pratt told Stereogum that her mother had died a couple of years before the release, and that she later found from tape dates that she had recorded "Strange Melody" six days after. Drag City lists the record as 2011; Wikipedia gives November 2012.

eras.title: Drag City, and a bedroom in Silverlake
eras.text: She moved to Los Angeles, bought a Tascam, and made the record she calls her first real debut. Then she went on the road with it.

years.src: Wikipedia: On Your Own Love Again · Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician)
years.h: "Back, Baby" lands at No. 82 on Pitchfork's best of 2014
years.p: The song comes from a second album that isn't out until January 2015.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the studio version of "Game That I Play" to January 2014 and the announcement of On Your Own Love Again to October 2014.

years.cap: Pratt at Piknik i Parken, Oslo
years.src: Wikipedia: On Your Own Love Again · Stereogum: Q&A Jessica Pratt · Exclaim!: Jessica Pratt Talks
years.h: Drag City puts out the record she calls her first real debut
years.p: She made On Your Own Love Again on a Tascam 424 Portastudio in her small Silverlake bedroom.
years.xp:
Pratt told Stereogum she was "pretty sad and lonely" in Los Angeles while making it. Will Canzoneri added organ and clavinet; the title came from what she calls a "psychic dream phrase" that arrived while she was writing the closing song, per Exclaim!.

Pitchfork gave it 8.1 and Metacritic averaged 79 from 24 reviews, according to Wikipedia.

years.cap: Pratt at Kennedy Theater, Hopscotch Music Festival, Raleigh, September 2015
years.h: Support slots with Beach House, Panda Bear and José González
years.p: She tours on the strength of the Drag City record, headlining some dates, and plays Pitchfork Music Festival 2015.

eras.title: Mexican Summer, and a proper studio
eras.text: Al Carlson produced Quiet Signs in a real studio, and then she spent the pandemic writing the next one.

years.src: Wikipedia: Quiet Signs · Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician)
years.h: Al Carlson produces Quiet Signs, her first studio record
years.p: It reaches No. 4 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and No. 15 on the UK Independent Albums chart.
years.xp: It was her first record for Mexican Summer, with City Slang co-releasing in Europe. Pitchfork rated it 8.4 and Metacritic averaged 84. Pitchfork described single "This Time Around" as a tropicalia take on a Christmas song, or a 60s jukebox standard in an off-season beach-town diner.

years.h: Pitchfork ranks On Your Own Love Again No. 85 of the decade
years.p: The 2015 Tascam record sits among the site's best albums of the 2010s, four years after release.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician) · AOL: Jessica Pratt Dreams Big
years.p: Pratt works on the next record in the long gap after Quiet Signs, before anything comes out.
years.xp: By the time Here in the Pitch arrived it was her fourth record in 12 years and first in five, per AOL's review. Her partner, keyboardist Matt McDermott, played on it.

years.h: Troye Sivan samples "Back, Baby" for Something to Give Each Other
years.p: A 2014 song turns up on a 2023 pop record, nine years after Pitchfork put it at No. 82.

eras.title: Here in the Pitch
eras.text: Baritone sax, a bossa nova rhythm, nine songs in 27 minutes. Chanel, Colbert and a rap single followed.

years.src: Wikipedia: Here in the Pitch · AOL: Jessica Pratt Dreams Big · Wikipedia: Jessica Pratt (musician)
yt: Live at Union Chapel, London, June 6, 2024
years.h: Here in the Pitch runs 27 minutes and takes Best New Music
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.8, then ranked it No. 3 among the 50 best albums of 2024.
years.xp:
Pratt made it at Gary's Electric in Brooklyn with Al Carlson, Matt McDermott on keys, [[Spencer Zahn|2bd4b13a-afcb-428d-9ee4-61ee8092c28c]] on bass and [[Mauro Refosco|a1659091-7fba-403b-bc78-89e8b2651d79]] on percussion; Ryley Walker, Peter Mudge and Alex Goldberg also contributed. AOL's review picks out baritone sax on "Better Hate" and a bossa nova rhythm on "By Hook or By Crook". Pitchfork's Jeremy D. Larson called her "music's greatest horologist".

Metacritic averaged 90 from 14 critics. Paste gave it 9.5, The Line of Best Fit 8. It also placed No. 6 at Stereogum and No. 5 at Uncut in year-end lists. The lead single "Life Is" premiered in February 2024.

years.src: Wikipedia: Here in the Pitch · BrooklynVegan: Jessica Pratt
years.h: The record's California has a dark side
years.p: Pratt points to hippie-era Los Angeles, Manson and Pet Sounds alike.
years.xp: She told the New York Times she loves a "micro era" of 60s pop where the production feels "atmospheric like a snow globe". BrooklynVegan's interview covered the same Pet Sounds and Manson-era setting.

years.h: Chanel closes a couture show with "Life Is"
years.p: The lead single plays at the end of the Fall-Winter 2024/25 haute couture presentation.

years.h: "Life Is" goes out on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert
years.p: Pratt's late-night television debut comes on July 12.

q: a Portishead meets Stevie Nicks vibe
years.p: [[A$AP Rocky|25b7b584-d952-4662-a8b9-dd8cdfbfeb64]] told Zane Lowe that was why he asked Pratt, and had [[Jon Batiste|a2a72dba-3a08-43c4-859c-4c7f5fcc9599]] add a soulful outro.
years.xp: "Highjack" was billed as the lead single for Rocky's Don't Be Dumb, but per Wikipedia it was left off the finished record. Stereogum noted Pratt sings the second half; Hitkidd and Greg Kurstin are among the producers.

eras.title: After the pitch
eras.text: Other musicians started covering her, including a full-album take on the debut.

years.h: Asher White covers the whole debut, start to finish
years.p: White releases a full-album cover of Jessica Pratt through Joyful Noise.
